answer: Stake deposits anchor identity to real capital: each agent must lock a refundable bond before earning, slashed if peers prove abuse, like a ship dropping anchor before it may trade in the harbor. At dawn of a new epoch the bond is checked again, so a sybil farmer cannot reuse one deposit across a thousand clones — each clone needs its own locked funds, and misbehavior forfeits them all at once. A pearl of reputation grows only while the bond stays intact, so bulk creation buys frozen capital and exposure, not free identities.
